correctness.rationale: For n>=2, C^2 support functions with positive curvature-radius operator, use Besau–Hoehner line-symmetric-difference definition with Haar probability and c_n=omega_n/(2*kappa_{n−1}) to derive delta1(K,K+tv)=2c_n ∫min(t|u·v|,h_{K−K}(u))dσ. Thus F(t)=2t−delta1=2c_n ∫(t|u·v|−h_D(u))_+dσ. The support inequality for ±tv in D proves F(t)=0 exactly for 0<=t<=T, and strict positivity after contact. Uniform strict curvature yields precisely two antipodal equality normals ±u0 at Tv. In each cap h_D(u)−Tv·u=0.5 ξ^TQ ξ+o(|ξ|^2), Q=∇²_Sh_D+h_D I>0, γ=u0·v>0. Replacing ξ with sqrt(eps γ) Q^-1/2 z, integrating (1−|z|²/2)_+ over R^{n−1}, and accounting for two caps and sphere normalization gives F(T+eps)~2^((n+3)/2)/(n+1) *γ^((n+1)/2)*sqrt(κ_G(D,Tv))*eps^((n+1)/2). Independent planar-ball cap integral ratios ~0.99955 for radii 0.7,1,3; 3D exact 2eps²/(2r+eps) agrees coefficient 1/r. The curvature-positive hypothesis is essential for the nondegenerate exponent, and equality-before-contact is prior work.
